## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `69addfe985db2a23e1754db183382010ed3a1377`
Local-runs: probe — one node script calling `governedTierFor` and `readLowRiskTier` from a `git show` copy of this head's `scripts/` tree, to measure the break cases the card names (trailing text, duplicated declarations, the `Metadata-protocol:` line, an unread changeset, non-wording shapes under `skills/`, a fork pull); no self-test, build or gate re-run
Scope: .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/lanes/skills.md, AGENTS.md + scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs, scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs

Inputs: card #33501 (body, claim, grading comment 6885437809, os-dev-report 6886128572), PR #33531 (body, five files, net diff against `main` from merge base 811b976a), and the check-runs on this head. The ruling quoted on the card: 「同意 把低风险的 Tier H 放权给座位」 and 「把低风险的 Tier H 放权给座位，立 p1 卡优化」. Its scope, in the coordinator's words on the card: pure docs, ADR notes and skills wording land on the seat's own contract-review PASS; anything touching a contract (spec or published types, Clause ②, narrowing) or security stays with the maintainer. Fail closed everywhere.

Check-runs on `69addfe9` at render time: 25 success, 26 skipped, 1 in progress (`Test Core (1/8)`), 0 failed. `Governed Surface Queue Guard` (pull_request leg), `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Check Changeset` and `PR-body guards` are green. The record does not say every check is green, because one shard is still running.

### ① Derived judgments

- `GOVERNED_SURFACES`: the `skills-catalog` and `ui-skills-catalog` rows keep `tier: H` and gain `lowRisk` (objectstack only). This is right: every path-only reader (CODEOWNERS mirror, `--test`, `--branch`, the prose gate, the relay's review plan) answers as before, as comment 6885437809 point 2 asked.
- `governedTierFor` and `testVerdict` take an optional `lowRisk` reading, and a caller that passes none gets the old answer. Right.
- New exports in the register: `LOW_RISK_ARM_RULING`, `LOW_RISK_RIDER_PATTERNS`, `lowRiskArmVerdict`, `applyLowRiskArm`, `renderLowRiskLines`, `pullLowRiskReading`. The register now imports `readClause2Line` from `clause2-line.mjs`, which is the fleet's one reader, not a second parser. Right.
- Queue guard: `decomposeGovernedWork` entries gain `allPaths`, every path of every commit attributed to the PR, collected before the governed filter, and `workflowDiff`. `makePullReader` now returns label names. `readLowRiskTier` is new. Right in shape.
- The accept set that widens: on `merge_group`, a PR whose only governed paths are under the catalog rows now clears on a seat enqueue plus a same-head `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` record, with no approval. The widening is in line with the ruling for skills wording. It is wrong where the reading admits things the ruling keeps with the maintainer (M1, S1 to S4 below).

### ② Semver level

Nothing in the diff publishes. The changed files are `scripts/pm/**`, `.claude/**` and `AGENTS.md`. `skip-changeset` is correct, and `Check Changeset` is green.

Clause-②: no

No published accept set or public surface moves. The changed exports belong to unpublished fleet tooling.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Open question (the `docs/adr/**` arm): leaving `docs/adr/**` at Tier H is the right call. The card body says "Do not decide it in code without the seat's word", and a path list cannot tell an ADR note from a changed decision. Option B (add-only, no Status line, nothing under a Decision heading) is the right next step, as its own card. The ADR half of the ruling is therefore still not delivered: ADR notes keep waiting on a maintainer click until that card lands. Option C, a self-declared line on the seat's record, is rightly rejected. Escalated to the seat: file the B card before #33501 closes on `Fixes`.
- Out-of-scope finding (the relay's `governedReviewPlan` still summons the approvers): agreed that it is a summons, not a block. It needs a follow-up card, and the seat files it.
- Observation, code outside the diff that this record reads but does not review: the Tier S record leg checks only that a record exists and where it came from. It never reads the verdict, and its own self-test pins that a FAIL record still clears. AGENTS.md PD 14 and this PR's header both say "a PASS verdict", but at the queue the arm actually rests on "a same-head record exists". This was true before for `.claude/**`, and the arm now extends it to the published catalog. Escalated to the seat to decide whether a follow-up card should make the queue leg read the verdict.
- Dev deviation (1), the model tier: met by this record at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`.

### ④ Design judgment

**M1 — must-fix. The arm reads contract declarations from the one carrier a seat can still change after the PASS, and leaves the committed carriers unread.** `lowRiskArmVerdict` in `check-governed-merges.mjs` decides "touches a contract" only from the PR body's `Clause-②:` value:
- (a) `LOW_RISK_RIDER_PATTERNS` admits any `.changeset/*.md` without reading it. The docblock says "a changeset (the one the published catalog owes)", but the code takes any package at any level. The probe read a skills diff plus an unread changeset as S. Under `.changeset/config.json` the catalog sits in one fixed train of about 120 packages, so a changeset that names another package, or grades a level above `patch`, is a release decision. It is not skills wording. The card lists "a `.changeset` that bumps a package other than `@objectstack/skills`" as a case that must fall back to Tier H.
- (b) The arm never reads the `Metadata-protocol:` line. The probe read `Clause-②: no` with `Metadata-protocol: semantic` as S. According to its own header, `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` refuses `added` under `no` and `narrowed` without the `(narrowing)` arm, but not `semantic`. A declared change of protocol meaning is a contract change under ruling A, and on this path it lands on the seat.
- (c) The body is not bound to the record. On `merge_group` the guard reads the live body, while the record pins only the head sha, and the recognisers never read a `Clause-②:` line from the record. A body edited from `yes` to `no` after a PASS therefore moves the PR from H to S, and the record still stands. The card's note asks exactly this: nothing a seat writes after the PASS should count without a fresh review.

Fix: in both `--pr` and the queue leg, read the PR's committed changesets at the head sha. The queue leg already reads committed trees for the workflow split. Require at least one changeset; each one must grade only `'@objectstack/skills': patch` and carry a bare `no` on its own Clause-② line and `none` on its `Metadata-protocol:` line. Keep the body check as an additional AND, and add a body `Metadata-protocol: none` check through `readMetadataProtocolLine`, the sibling reader in `clause2-line.mjs`. Pin each case in both batteries.

**S1 — should-fix. Removing the `security` label after the record moves the PR to S.** The arm reads only the labels the PR carries at queue time. Adding the label after the record correctly falls back to H. Removing it before the enqueue gives S, and no fresh review is needed for that. Fix: read the timeline, which the enqueue leg already fetches for every unapproved entry, and treat any `unlabeled` event for `security` on the PR as H.

**S2 — should-fix. Clause-② lines with trailing text, or more than one Clause-② line, read S.** `readClause2Line` takes the first line that matches and ignores the rest. The probe read all of these as S: a `no` followed by an em-dash and a sentence saying it narrows the spec; a `no` followed by a parenthesis that does not start with an arm word; a `no` line followed later by a `yes` line; a `no` inside a blockquote followed by a real `yes`; and a `no` inside a code fence followed by a real `yes`. The card names "duplicated" and "carries trailing text" as cases that must be H. Fix: without adding a second parser, run the one reader once per line, refuse more than one declared or malformed line, and require that nothing but decoration follows the value.

**S3 — should-fix. A fork PR passes the arm.** `pullLowRiskReading` and `readLowRiskTier` never look at the head repository. The probe gave S for a pull whose `head.repo` is null, which is a deleted fork. PD 14 says a fork PR is never a delivery. The arm opens the published catalog, the surface an outside contributor is most likely to send, and nothing in the record leg checks who wrote the record. Fix: `makePullReader` and `pullLowRiskReading` should take `head.repo.full_name` and `base.repo.full_name` from the pull object they already fetch, and a fork, or an unread head repo, should be H. `forkVerdict` already exists in the register.

**S4 — should-fix. Inside the arm rows, anything under `skills/` counts as wording.** The rider list is an allowlist of path shapes, but the arm rows are matched by prefix alone. The probe read `skills/objectstack-data/src/x.ts` and `skills/package.json` as S. The card names "any `src/`". Skills shipped by `npx skills add` can carry scripts that a customer's agent runs, and the first PR that adds one would land on the seat. Fix: allow only `.md` files and `evals/*.json` under the arm rows, which covers every file under `skills/` on `main` today. Anything else should be H.

**N1 — nit.** PD 14 names `lowRiskArmVerdict` but does not say that the arm reads `Clause-②`, labels and paths, and does not cite the ruling. Card item 3 asked for the ruling to be cited. The phrase "objectstack workflow edits ... and skills wording" also leaves it ambiguous whether "objectstack" covers the skills arm, though the code scopes it to objectstack. This is prose only, so it can be fixed on AGENTS.md or left as an accepted deviation.

**N2 — nit.** `SKILL.md` line 202 drops the H triggers for workflows (published path, C2 trigger, refused read) and keeps only "未读 ⇒ H", pointing to the script header. That is acceptable under the pointer rule, but a seat reading only the skill now sees less of the rule than before.

Holds, read against the code:
- The guard takes the body and labels from the pull object it already fetches, with no read of its own.
- An unreadable pull, unread labels, an empty body, a missing `Clause-②:` line, `yes`, `(narrowing)` and `(widening)` are all H.
- A record on an older head is refused.
- Each other governed row beside the catalog is H: `docs/adr/**`, `docs/NORTH-STAR.md`, `.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md`, and a split workflow row, because the arm runs after `applyWorkflowSplit`.
- `packages/**`, `ui/packages/**`, gate scripts, lockfiles and non-Markdown docs are H.
- A published path in another commit of the same PR counts through `allPaths`.
- The `pull_request` leg never reddens.
- The CODEOWNERS mirror and every path-only caller answer exactly as before.
- `check:pm-governed-prose` agrees with PD 14 on the surface list (green in CI). It deliberately does not parse tier words, so the tier sentence is judged here: it does not go beyond the ruling. It is narrower, since it covers skills wording only and leaves docs/ADR out.
- The post-merge sweep still lists every catalog merge, as it does every `.claude/**` merge. Card item 4 is met to the same standard: in both cases a merge without a PASS record is a finding for the human audit.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-dhp24e`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Correction: contract-review tier

The contract-review record(s) 6886243839 on this PR say `Served-tier: CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, and the seat adopted them as "isolated sub-agent at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER". **That is wrong.** The seat launched the reviewing sub-agent without the tier, so it ran at the seat's own default tier, not at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. The seat found this on its own audit. The review was still isolated and adversarial, and its findings stand as an off-tier review. They are not the at-tier record AGENTS.md and the in-seat review ruling require.

The seat re-runs the review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on this PR's head and posts that record here. Until it does, this PR has no at-tier record.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4a459236f421a0add59431b816de104de054eb89`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/lanes/skills.md, AGENTS.md + scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs, scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs, scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs

Inputs: card #33501 (body, claim 6885432460, grading comment 6885437809, os-dev-report 6886128572), PR #33531 (the r2 body as the dev's file reads, six files, net diff against `main` from merge base e3f0cfd4), and the check-runs on this head. This is a full review of the reworked head. The earlier record 6886243839 is not used as evidence; ③ says which of its findings this review confirms as fixed.

The ruling quoted on the card: 「同意 把低风险的 Tier H 放权给座位」 and 「把低风险的 Tier H 放权给座位，立 p1 卡优化」. Its scope, in the coordinator's words on the card: pure docs, ADR notes and skills wording land on the seat's own contract-review PASS; anything touching a contract (spec or published types, Clause ②, narrowing) or security stays with the maintainer.

Check-runs on `4a459236` at render time: 22 success, 22 skipped, 2 in progress (`Test Core (1/8)`, `Type Check · consumer gates`), 0 failed. Every Lint job is green, among them `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates` and `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` (pull_request leg) and `PR-body guards` are green; `Check Changeset` is an expected skip under `skip-changeset`. This record does not say every check is green: two shards were still running, neither of them a gate over the files in scope.

### ① Derived judgments

- `GOVERNED_SURFACES`: the `skills-catalog` and `ui-skills-catalog` rows keep `tier: H` and gain `lowRisk`, scoped to objectstack. Right. Every path-only reader (`--test`, `--branch`, the CODEOWNERS mirror, the prose gate, the relay's review plan, the post-merge sweep) answers as before, which is what comment 6885437809 point 2 asked for.
- `governedTierFor` and `testVerdict` take one more optional argument. A caller that hands no reading gets Tier H on a catalog path. Right, and it is the fail-closed default.
- New register exports: `LOW_RISK_ARM_RULING`, `LOW_RISK_RIDER_PATTERNS`, `LOW_RISK_ARM_FILE_PATTERNS`, `LOW_RISK_CHANGESET_PATH`, `LOW_RISK_CHANGESET_RELEASE`, `readBareDeclaration`, `lowRiskChangesetReasons`, `lowRiskArmVerdict`, `applyLowRiskArm`, `renderLowRiskLines`, `pullLowRiskReading`, `lowRiskRowHit`, `fetchTimelineOver`, `pullChangesetReading`. The declarations are read with `readClause2Line` and `readMetadataProtocolLine` from `clause2-line.mjs`, run once per line. Right: no second parser.
- Queue guard: `decomposeGovernedWork` entries gain `allPaths`, `changesetRefs` and `workflowDiff`; `makePullReader` returns label names and `forkVerdict`; new `readLowRiskTier`, `landsOnLowRiskArm`, `lowRiskRecordVerdict`; a new record state `not-pass`, which every clearing predicate (`state === 'stands'`) refuses. Right.
- `record-recognisers.mjs` re-exports `contractReviewVerdictOf`, which it already imported. Right: one verdict reader, reached by the guard's lazy loader as `verdictOf`.
- The accept set that widens: on `merge_group`, a PR whose only governed paths are catalog paths clears on a seat enqueue with zero approvals when the arm reads Tier S and the same-head record reads PASS. That is the ruling's skills-wording arm and nothing wider, with the one gap in SF1. Nothing narrows for any other entry: the other Tier S legs and every Tier H leg read as on `main`.

### ② Semver level

Nothing in the diff publishes: `scripts/pm/**`, `.claude/**` and `AGENTS.md`. `skip-changeset` is correct.

Clause-②: no

No published accept set or public surface moves; the changed exports belong to unpublished fleet tooling.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Open question, the `docs/adr/**` arm: leaving it Tier H is the right call under the ruling. The card says not to decide it in code without the seat's word, a path cannot tell a note from a changed decision, and fail closed is the ruling's own default. The ADR half of the ruling is therefore not delivered by this PR; #33539 (open) carries it, so `Fixes #33501` does not lose it. Option C, a self-declared line on the seat's record, stays rejected.
- Out-of-scope finding, the relay's `governedReviewPlan`: a summons, not a block. #33540 (open) carries it. Agreed.
- The other Tier S legs still read no verdict: #33541 (open) carries it. Agreed that it is outside this card.
- Dev deviation (1), the model tier: met by this record.
- Findings of record 6886243839, judged on this tree:
  - M1 (a), changesets unread: fixed. Both `--pr` and the queue leg read each changed changeset from a committed tree; at least one is required; the frontmatter may hold only the catalog at patch; an unread, deleted or frontmatter-less changeset is H.
  - M1 (b), `Metadata-protocol:` unread: fixed, on the body and on each changeset.
  - M1 (c), the body not bound to the record: fixed in part. The body is now a redundant AND over the committed changeset, so a body edit alone moves nothing from H to S. The committed carrier is itself not bound to the record: see SF1.
  - S1, a removed `security` label: fixed. The guard keeps the timeline the enqueue leg already read (every page or it throws); `--pr` reads every page or says NOT MEASURED.
  - S2, trailing text and duplicated declarations: fixed. Exactly one declaration line, outside a fence and a quote, equal to the bare spelling after decoration is stripped.
  - S3, a fork head: fixed, through `forkVerdict` on the pull object both readers already fetch; a deleted head repo or an unread predicate is H.
  - S4, any file under the catalog rows: fixed. Only `.md` and `evals/*.json`, which covers all 97 files under `skills/` on this head.
  - Its observation that the record leg read no verdict: fixed for the arm (`lowRiskRecordVerdict`), newest same-head record governs.
  - N1 not taken, with a reason that holds (AGENTS.md takes no ruling quotation; the conditions live in the script header PD 14 names). Accepted deviation. N2 fixed: the SKILL.md line keeps the workflow triggers.
- Escalated to the seat, not a finding on this diff: the arm's only security reading is the `security` label, as the card specifies, and no workflow applies that label by path. A skills PR that rewrites security teaching (for example `skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md`, the file #33480 changed) reads Tier S unless someone hangs the label. Whether the ruling's "security stays with the maintainer" means the label or the content is the seat's question to put to the maintainer; until it is answered the at-tier reviewer of such a PR should hang the label.

### ④ Design judgment

**SF1 — should-fix. On the arm, a carried record lets the declarations and catalog files move after the PASS.** The M1 fix makes the committed changeset the carrier of `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none` and the release line. The queue guard's record leg still accepts a record on an OLDER head when the head moved only on prose faces outside the review surface (`regenCarry` and `isOutsideReviewSurface` in `record-recognisers.mjs`: `.changeset/**`, `content/docs/**`, `apps/docs/**`, and any `CHANGELOG.md` at any depth), pointed at by a `Regen-provenance:` comment a seat writes. `lowRiskRecordVerdict` reads the verdict of that carried record and does not look at `carriedHops`. Two consequences, both read off the code, neither pinned by a self-test:
- (a) Head A carries `Clause-②: yes` (or a non-`none` protocol kind, or a release line beyond the catalog at patch) on the body and the changeset, so it is Tier H, and the record on A is written against that declaration. The seat then rewrites the changeset to the clean spelling at head B, edits the body to match, and posts the provenance line. At the queue the arm reads the body and the changeset at B, answers Tier S, the record carries, reads PASS, and the seat's enqueue clears. Both declaration carriers were written after the PASS and no review saw them. This is the card note's "an edited body after the record" case, and it does not fall back to Tier H.
- (b) `skills/**/CHANGELOG.md` is a `.md` under a catalog row, so the arm admits it, and it is also on the carry's excluded list by basename, so catalog content added or changed after the PASS lands on the carried record.
The exposure is bounded: the path allowlist and the release line are still read at the queued commit, so no published source, schema or package bump can ride through. What is lost is the tripwire the ruling names (Clause ②) and the same-head guarantee for one file name under the catalog. Fix, in `lowRiskRecordVerdict` or beside it and through the readers already imported: on an arm entry refuse a carried record whose hops moved any `.changeset/` path or any path under a catalog row (or refuse every carried record on the arm, which costs a fresh review after a merge-forward), and pin both cases in the queue battery. Reading the record's own Clause-② line with `readClause2Line` and requiring bare `no` is a second, independent way to bind (a).

**N1 — nit.** PD 14 and SKILL.md line 202 name the arm beside `.claude/**` under Tier S, and neither says the arm is exclusive: skills wording beside a `.claude/**` path is Tier H in the code (`a governed path outside the arm`), where a reader of the prose would expect S plus S. The error direction is safe, since `--pr` answers H. Prose only; fix on the prose faces or leave as an accepted deviation.

**N2 — nit.** The `ui-skills-catalog` row carries the arm, but the arm's one allowed release line is `'@objectstack/skills': patch` in a root `.changeset/*.md`, and `ui/.changeset/**` is not a rider. No `ui/skills/` tree exists on this head, so nothing is reachable today; when one appears the arm either never fires or fires on a changeset that names the wrong package. A follow-up card when `ui/skills/**` gets its first file.

**N3 — nit.** The post-merge sweep classifies by path alone, so a seat-landed arm merge is listed as a Tier H row with no approval, and the auditor has to re-read the arm by hand to tell it from a violation. Card item 4 is met at parity with `.claude/**` (the merge is on the list, and a missing PASS record is the human audit's finding), no better. Follow-up card material.

**N4 — nit.** Comments in both scripts cite 6886243839 as "contract review"; that record was served off-tier and is being replaced. The pointers describe history accurately, but they should name the record that stands. Accepted deviation on this head, since a comment edit moves it.

Holds, read against the code and each tried as a break:
- Published source or any path outside the allowlist: `packages/**`, `ui/packages/**`, a gate script, a lockfile, `.changeset/config.json`, a nested `.changeset/a/b.md`, a non-Markdown file under `docs/` or `content/docs/`, `ui/docs/**` are each H. The list is an allowlist of shapes, so the next published tree is H without an edit.
- A rename out of published source into `skills/` is H: `--pr` reads `previous_filename`, and the guard's rows are `diff-tree --no-renames`, so both paths reach the allowlist. A published path in another commit of the same PR counts through `allPaths`, collected before the governed filter.
- Under the catalog rows: `.js`, `.mjs`, `.sh`, `.yaml`, `.png`, `package.json`, and `evals/sub/*.json` are H.
- The body: no line, `yes`, any arm, `no` with trailing words, two declaration lines (two `no` included), a quoted or fenced `no` beside a real `yes`, a lone quoted or fenced `no`, a missing or non-`none` `Metadata-protocol:` line, and a body that is not a string are each H. A hidden declaration cannot be undercounted: every line the fleet reader reads as declared or malformed is a hit, fenced or not, and the final test is equality with the bare spelling.
- The changeset: none, another package, the catalog above patch, a second release line, an indented or commented frontmatter line, no frontmatter, a deleted or unreadable one, a second changeset the reading holds no file for, and a missing or annotated declaration are each H. The frontmatter bounds agree with the changesets parser's own.
- Labels and timeline: a `security` label in any case, labels not read, an `unlabeled` event for it, a timeline that threw, was cut, or was never read are each H. A label added after the record is read live at the queue and is H.
- A fork head, a deleted head repository and an unread fork predicate are H. An unreadable pull is NOT MEASURED and H.
- Any other governed row beside the catalog is H: `docs/adr/**`, `docs/NORTH-STAR.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/**`, and a split workflow row, because the arm runs after `applyWorkflowSplit`.
- A record on an older head with no provenance line is refused; a same-head FAIL, a record with no verdict word, a newer FAIL behind an older PASS and a missing verdict reader are each refused as `not-pass`.
- The guard reads the body, labels and fork predicate from the pull object it already fetches and the timeline from the read the enqueue leg already makes; it adds no API call of its own. The `merge_group` job checks out with full history and blobs, so `git show` of a changeset at its commit reads in production. The `pull_request` leg says Tier H, NOT MEASURED, and never reddens.
- `check:pm-governed-prose` is green in `lint.yml` on this head and PD 14's surface list is unchanged. The gate does not parse tier words, so the tier sentence is judged here: "every register row outside Tier S" and "skills wording (`lowRiskArmVerdict`) read as S" do not widen beyond the ruling. They are narrower: docs prose was never governed and ADR notes stay H.
- `SKILL.md`: the two edited lines agree with the register on this head (the tier is a reading, not a path fact; both readers named, the workflow H triggers kept, unread is H), within the line budget. `references/lanes/skills.md`: `--pr N` is the right pre-arm command, since `--test` and `--branch` can never read the arm; it names the fetch that cures an unread head. The other pm-dispatch lines the card listed speak of the tiers generically and still hold.
- The r2 body's account matches the tree where checked: battery floors 54 and 38, AGENTS.md 1050 lines on both sides, SKILL.md 319 lines, the three follow-up cards exist and are open.

## Contract review
